messages:
hz: Heads-up: large-tenant rollout revealed policy compile latency spike when overlays apply. We need a low-risk plan.
mina: Can we avoid compiling on every read? We currently merge+compile per request if TTL expired.
omar: Suggestion: keep merged compiled blobs cached by generation id, invalidate on overlay update. For updates, do async recompile and serve previous blob until new is ready.
hz: Async compile sounds safest but we also need a detection for when the compiled blob is incompatible with runtime after deploy.
mina: Add a compiler-version marker and invariants-hash to blobs. Runtime rejects unknown marker and falls back to core_policy. Log audit event for "incompatible-compiled-policy".
omar: For overlays, enforce that they are single-field deltas (region_preference, max_cost_multiplier, burst_allowance). No references to penalty functions or admission filters. That keeps dependency graph tiny so async compile is safe.
hz: Ops+SRE want visibility. Emit policy-compile-duration, merge-latency, and active-compiled-blobs count.
build-bot: note: created ticket POL-189: cached-compiled-blobs + async-recompile.
mina: Also add a preview API that returns merged YAML and simulated metrics for a sample trace. That avoids surprise rollouts.
hz: Action items: omar -> async compiler prototype (WIP Tue); mina -> preview API stub (end of week); hz -> RFC snippet for allowed overlay fields (tomorrow).
omar: Will also include a fallback mode where runtime silently serves core_policy and flags tenant for manual review.
hz: Cool. If we keep overlays narrow and compile async, we should avoid the 100ms-per-request penalty.
